mainTopic: Conditional גיטין: a condition to marry a named man, impossible conditions, and forbidden conditions
overview: The amud opens by finishing an earlier discussion. Once a husband fully frees his wife, even for a short time, the גט works according to both רבי אליעזר and the רבנן. Next comes a ברייתא about a גט given 'on condition that you marry so-and-so.' רב נחמן tries two readings of it, and רבא knocks down the second, including a comparison to a vow about sleeping. רבא then gives his own reading, and a ברייתא backs him up. Before the fact, she may marry neither the named man nor anyone else. After the fact, she stays with the named man but must leave any other man. Then a ברייתא brings conditions no one can fulfill, like going up to the sky. רבי יהודה בן תימא says the husband was only exaggerating, so the גט is valid, and the הלכה follows him. Last, אביי and רבא argue whether a forbidden condition, like eating בשר חזיר, counts as impossible. רבא defends his view against a ברייתא about relations with 'my father or your father.'

steps.title: Once he cuts her off, she is cut off
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes the earlier question. If the husband fully frees his wife, even for a limited time, the separation is real according to both רבי אליעזר and the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense that according to both רבי אליעזר and the רבנן, once he has cut her off, she is cut off.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wraps up the discussion from before this section. A husband who completely frees his wife has truly ended the marriage, and every opinion agrees.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר and the רבנן argue about a גט that leaves the wife forbidden to someone. Here, though, the husband made her fully free, even if only for a time. That complete break is enough to dissolve the marriage, so the earlier argument does not matter for this case.

keyTerms.meaning: It stands to reason; it makes sense
Both according to ... and according to ...
Once he has cut her off, she is cut off

steps.whatToRemember: A complete break, even a temporary one, counts as a real divorce according to everyone.

phrases.aramaic: מִסְתַּבְּרָא, בֵּין לְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֵּין לְרַבָּנַן,
phrases.english: It stands to reason, both according to Rabbi Eliezer and according to the Rabbis,
once he has cut her off, he has cut her off.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִסְתַּבְּרָא, בֵּין לְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֵּין לְרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the discussion that began before this section.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: When a husband completely frees his wife, the divorce takes effect according to both רבי אליעזר and the רבנן.

steps.title: A divorce on condition that she marry a certain man
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules on a גט given on the condition that she marry a specific man. She should not marry, but if she does, she need not leave.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: if a man says, 'Here is your גט on condition that you marry so-and-so,' she should not marry. But if she did marry, she does not have to leave.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic by quoting a ברייתא about a גט with an unusual condition. The ברייתא's wording is unclear, and the גמרא is about to ask about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling has two parts: she should not marry from the start, but after the fact the marriage stands. The ברייתא never says whom she may not marry, the named man or anyone else. That missing detail sets up the next question.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages taught; opens a ברייתא

phrases.english: The Sages taught: 'This is your bill of divorce
on condition that you marry so-and-so'
she may not marry,
but if she married, she need not leave.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הֲרֵי זֶה גִּיטִּיךְ עַל מְנָת שֶׁתִּנָּשְׂאִי לִפְלוֹנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the conclusion in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With a גט 'on condition you marry so-and-so,' she should not marry from the start, but if she did, she may stay married.

steps.title: What does the ברייתא mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the ברייתא is saying, since it does not say whom she may not marry.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is it saying?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a clearer reading of the unclear ברייתא. This question sets up רב נחמן's explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'She may not marry' could mean the named man or anyone at all. The גמרא needs to know which, because it changes the whole case.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it saying?; a request to explain unclear wording

phrases.english: What is it saying?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the unclear wording of the ברייתא in step 2.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whom does 'she may not marry' refer to, and whom does 'if she married' refer to?

steps.title: רב נחמן: she may not marry the named man
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן explains that she may not marry the named man, so people won't say men give their wives away as gifts. If she marries someone else, she need not leave.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said, this is what it means: she may not marry him, the man named in the condition, because people might say men give their wives to each other as gifts. And if she married someone else, she does not have to leave.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן answers the question. 'She may not marry' means the named man, and 'if she married' means a different man.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Marrying the named man is forbidden by a rabbinic גזירה. It might look like husbands are passing their wives around as presents. So the case where she married and need not leave must be about someone other than the named man.

keyTerms.meaning: Lest people say; a worry about how things look
They give their wives as a gift

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said, this is what it is saying:
she may not marry him,
phrases.notes: 'Him' is the man named in the condition, the פלוני.

phrases.english: lest people say they give their wives as a gift.
And if she married another man, she need not leave.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: She is forbidden to marry the named man because of a גזירה about how it looks. If she married a different man, she may stay with him.

steps.title: Can a rabbinic decree permit a married woman?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא attacks רב נחמן. If she married someone other than the named man, the condition was never met and she is still an אשת איש, so how can we let her stay?
steps.simpleTranslation: And because of a rabbinic decree we do not take her away from him, and we let a married woman marry anyone?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב נחמן's reading. It says his reading leads to a result that cannot be right.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גט only works if she marries the named man. Under רב נחמן, the rabbis forbade that very marriage, so she married someone else, and the condition was never fulfilled. By תורה law she is still an אשת איש. It seems impossible that a rabbinic גזירה would end up letting her live with another man.

keyTerms.meaning: A rabbinic decree made as a safeguard
We take her away from him

steps.confusionAlert: The problem is not the גזירה itself. The problem is that the גזירה blocks the condition from ever being met, so the גט never took effect.

phrases.english: And because of a decree, we do not take her away from him,
phrases.notes: 'Him' here is the other man she married, not the one named in the condition.

phrases.english: and we permit a married woman to anyone?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב נחמן's explanation from step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's reading that she may stay married to another man.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under his reading, the condition to marry the named man was never fulfilled, so the גט never took effect. She remains an אשת איש by תורה law, and a rabbinic גזירה cannot be the reason a married woman is allowed to another man.

steps.title: רב נחמן's new reading: she should not marry the named man
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן drops his first explanation. Now he reads the ברייתא as forbidding her to marry the named man himself, so people won't say men give their wives away as gifts. If she did marry him, she stays, since we don't take a woman from her husband because of a גזרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב נחמן said, this is what the ברייתא means: she may not marry him, the named man, because people might say that men give their wives away as gifts. But if she did marry him, she does not have to leave, because we don't force a woman out of her marriage just because of a rabbinic decree.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן answers the קשיא from step 5 by switching to a new explanation of the ברייתא. Now both halves of the ruling are about marrying the named man.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 4, 'if she marries' meant marrying someone else, and that is what step 5 attacked. Now the problem case is marrying the named man himself, which fulfills the condition, so the גט is fully valid. The ban is only a rabbinic גזרה about appearances, and a גזרה like that is not strong enough to break up a marriage that has already happened.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather: drops the earlier explanation and gives a new one
A gift; here, the fear that people will say wives are passed around as gifts
We do not take her out of the marriage

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Nachman said,
this is what the ברייתא is saying:
she may not marry him,
phrases.notes: 'Him' is now the man named in the condition, not some other man.

phrases.english: lest people say
that men give their wives away as a gift.
But if she married him, she need not leave,
since we do not remove her because of a decree.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן, הָכִי קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 5 by replacing רב נחמן's first reading of the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the ברייתא: both the ban and 'she need not leave' refer to the named man
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא let her stay after marrying someone else, even though the condition was not met.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא lets her stay with the named man. The condition was fulfilled, and the ban is only a גזרה, which cannot undo a marriage.

steps.title: רבא: does this let her marry someone else first?
steps.stepSummary: רבא points out that if only the named man is forbidden, then marrying another man seems allowed. But she still has to fulfill the condition of marrying the named man.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: You are saying she may not marry him. That implies she may marry another man! But she still has to fulfill the condition!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא challenges רב נחמן's new reading. He draws an implication from it that seems wrong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the ברייתא forbids only the named man, it sounds like she can marry anyone else right away. But the גט only works once she marries the named man. Until then, marrying someone else is a problem, so how could that be allowed?

keyTerms.meaning: To another man, not the one named in the condition

phrases.english: Rava said to him:
It is to him that she may not be married,
implying that she may marry another man?!
But she needs to fulfill the condition!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the new reading given in step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's reading that only the named man is off-limits
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Forbidding only the named man implies other men are allowed. But until she fulfills the condition by marrying the named man, she cannot freely marry anyone else.

steps.title: Possible defense: marry today, divorce tomorrow
steps.stepSummary: רבא suggests an answer רב נחמן might give. She could marry another man today, get divorced tomorrow, and then still fulfill the condition. רבא links this to רב נחמן's known dispute with רב יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you would say: it is possible that she marries someone today and is divorced tomorrow, and then fulfills the condition. And you are comparing this to the case in which you disagree with רב יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא is setting up the next move. He states the answer רב נחמן might give so that he can examine it and later push back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that marrying another man does not ruin anything, because the condition can still be met later. רב נחמן does not worry that she will fail to fulfill it. רבא says this approach matches רב נחמן's own view in a dispute with רב יהודה, which the גמרא is about to quote.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say: introduces an answer someone might give

steps.confusionAlert: This is still רבא talking. He is not agreeing with this answer. He is laying it out so he can deal with it next.

phrases.english: And if you would say:
it is possible that she marries another man today
and is divorced tomorrow,
and then fulfills the condition;
and to that case where you disagree with Rav Yehuda
you are comparing it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא: אֶפְשָׁר דְּמִינַּסְבָא הַיּוֹם וּמִיגָּרְשָׁה לִמְחַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: States a possible answer to רבא's own קשיא in step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Anticipated defense: the condition can still be fulfilled later
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Marrying another man first blocks the condition from ever being met.
steps.terutzMaskana: She can marry, get divorced, and still marry the named man, so there is nothing to worry about now.

steps.title: The vow about sleeping today if he sleeps tomorrow
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the dispute. A man vows that sleep is forbidden to his eyes today if he sleeps tomorrow. רב יהודה says he may not sleep today, in case he sleeps tomorrow. רב נחמן says he may sleep today, and we don't worry that he will sleep tomorrow.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was stated: 'My eyes are קונם from sleep today if I sleep tomorrow.' רב יהודה said: he should not sleep today, in case he sleeps tomorrow. רב נחמן said: he may sleep today, and we don't worry that he will sleep tomorrow.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the dispute רבא just mentioned. This is the source the possible defense in step 8 rests on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Whether today's sleep is forbidden depends on what happens tomorrow. רב יהודה is strict now in case the condition kicks in later. רב נחמן trusts that the person will act so that no prohibition happens, just as the woman can still fulfill her condition later.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was stated: introduces a known dispute between אמוראים
A form of vow making something forbidden like a קרבן

steps.whyThisMatters: This dispute is about how to act now when a later event could make the action forbidden after the fact. That is the same question as the woman marrying before fulfilling her condition.

phrases.english: As it was stated:
'My eyes are konam from sleep today,'
'if I sleep tomorrow,'
Rav Yehuda said:
he should not sleep today,
lest he sleep tomorrow;
and Rav Nachman said:
he may sleep today,
and we are not concerned that he might sleep tomorrow;

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאִתְּמַר: קֻוֽנָּם עֵינַי בְּשֵׁינָה הַיּוֹם, אִם אִישַׁן לְמָחָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the dispute that step 8 said רב נחמן would compare to.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In a vow where today's sleep is forbidden only if he sleeps tomorrow, רב יהודה forbids sleeping today. רב נחמן allows it and does not worry about tomorrow.

steps.title: The sleep case is not like the marriage case
steps.stepSummary: רבא rejects the comparison to the sleep vow. A man can keep himself awake, but a woman cannot force her new husband to divorce her.
steps.simpleTranslation: How can you compare them?! There, it is up to him: if he wants, he can prick himself with thorns and stay awake. Here, is it up to her to get divorced?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא knocks down the suggestion from Step 8 that רב נחמן would let her marry another man today and divorce him tomorrow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the sleep case, the man fully controls whether the condition gets broken, so רב נחמן can trust him. In our case, once she marries another man, only he can give the divorce. She has no control, and she may never be free to fulfill the condition.

keyTerms.meaning: How can you compare? A phrase used to reject a comparison.
It is in his own hands, up to him.

phrases.english: How can these be compared?!
There, it is up to him,
phrases.notes: "There" means the sleep vow from Step 9.

phrases.english: for if he wants, he can prick himself with thorns,
and not fall asleep;
here, is it up to her to get divorced?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the comparison between the sleep vow (Step 9) and the marriage case that was made in Step 8.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggestion that רב נחמן's sleep ruling lets her marry another man before fulfilling the condition.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The sleep case is in the man's control. A divorce is not in the woman's control, so she might never be able to fulfill the condition.

steps.title: רבא's own reading of the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: רבא reads the ברייתא this way. Before the fact, she may marry neither the named man nor anyone else. After the fact, she stays if she married the named man, and she must leave if she married someone else.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: she may marry neither him nor another man. She may not marry him, so people won't say men give their wives away as gifts. She may not marry another man, because she still has to fulfill the condition. If she did marry him, she does not have to leave, because we don't take a woman from her husband over a גזרה. If she married another man, she must leave, because she still has to fulfill the condition.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a new explanation of the ברייתא. Each man gets his own reason, and there is a separate ruling for before the fact and after the fact.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Marrying the named man is only forbidden by a rabbinic גזרה about appearances. That is why, once she has married him, we leave her with him. Marrying another man is a real problem, because the condition of the גט is still not fulfilled. So even after the fact, she must leave him.

keyTerms.meaning: We take her out, meaning we separate her from her husband

steps.confusionAlert: Both men are forbidden before the fact, but for very different reasons. That is why the after-the-fact results are opposite: she stays with the named man, but she must leave the other man.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
This woman may not marry
not him, and not another man.
She may not marry him,
lest people say:
they give their wives as a gift;
she may not marry another man,
because she needs to fulfill the condition.
And if she married him, she does not leave,
for we do not take her out because of a decree;
if she married another man, she must leave,
because she needs to fulfill the condition.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the sleep comparison falls (Step 10), רבא offers a fresh reading of the ברייתא that answers his own question from Step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New reading of the ברייתא that forbids both men before the fact
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only the named man is forbidden, so marrying another man would be allowed.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both men are forbidden before the fact. After the fact, she stays with the named man because that ban is only a גזרה, but she must leave another man because the condition is still unfulfilled.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רבא
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא is quoted that says exactly what רבא said: neither man before the fact; after the fact, she stays with the named man and leaves another man.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא was taught that agrees with רבא: this woman may marry neither him nor another man. If she married him, she does not leave. If she married another man, she must leave.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that matches רבא's reading word for word, which backs him up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here a ברייתא openly states both parts of רבא's ruling, the before-the-fact ban and the after-the-fact split. This supports רבא's approach after the earlier attempts at explaining the ברייתא were rejected.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא was taught in agreement with him.

steps.whatToRemember: Final rule: a woman divorced on condition that she marry a named man may not marry him or anyone else before the fact. If she married him, she stays. If she married someone else, she must leave.

phrases.english: It was taught in a baraita in accordance with Rava:
This woman may not marry
not him and not another man,
and if she married him, she does not leave,
if she married another man, she must leave.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבא's reading from Step 11 with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's ruling that both men are forbidden before the fact, with different results after the fact.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that states the same ruling in full.

steps.title: A ברייתא: a גט with an impossible condition is not valid
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists conditions no human can fulfill. The first opinion rules that such a גט is not valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: If a man says, "This is your גט on condition that you go up to the sky," or go down to the depths, or swallow a four-אמה reed, or bring me a hundred-אמה reed, or cross the Great Sea on foot, it is not a גט.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic by quoting a ברייתא about conditions that are impossible to fulfill. The first opinion (תנא קמא) says the גט does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every example is something no person can ever do. The תנא קמא treats the condition as binding. Since it can never be fulfilled, the גט never takes effect.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
"This is your bill of divorce
on condition that you go up to the sky";
"on condition that you go down to the depths";

phrases.aramaic: ״עַל מְנָת שֶׁתִּבְלְעִי קָנֶה שֶׁל אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת״;
phrases.english: "on condition that you swallow a reed four cubits long";

phrases.aramaic: ״עַל מְנָת שֶׁתָּבִיאִי לִי קָנֶה בֶּן מֵאָה אַמָּה״;
phrases.english: "on condition that you bring me a reed a hundred cubits long";

phrases.aramaic: ״עַל מְנָת שֶׁתַּעַבְרִי אֶת הַיָּם הַגָּדוֹל בְּרַגְלַיִךְ״ –
phrases.english: "on condition that you cross the Great Sea on foot" —
it is not a bill of divorce.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הֲרֵי זֶה גִּיטִּךְ עַל מְנָת שֶׁתַּעֲלִי לָרָקִיעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, moving from conditions about whom she may marry to conditions that cannot be fulfilled.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the תנא קמא, a גט given on an impossible condition is not valid.

steps.title: רבי יהודה בן תימא: the גט is valid, because he was only exaggerating
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה בן תימא disagrees and says the גט works. His general rule is that an impossible condition is just empty talk.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה בן תימא says: A case like this is a valid גט. רבי יהודה בן תימא stated a rule: any condition that cannot be fulfilled in the end, which he set from the start, is only him exaggerating with words, and the גט is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: A second opinion in the same ברייתא disagrees with the תנא קמא. It says the גט is valid, and it gives a general rule for why.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה בן תימא reasons that nobody seriously makes a condition he knows can never happen. So the husband did not really mean it as a condition. We ignore the condition, and the גט works right away.

keyTerms.meaning: Like someone who is just exaggerating with words

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda ben Teima says:
A case like this is a valid bill of divorce.

phrases.aramaic: כְּלָל אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן תֵּימָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda ben Teima stated a general rule:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל תְּנַאי שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לוֹ לְקַיְּימוֹ בְּסוֹפוֹ,
phrases.english: any condition that cannot be fulfilled in the end,
and he set it as a condition from the start —
he is only like someone exaggerating with words,
and the divorce is valid.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן תֵּימָא אוֹמֵר: כָּזֶה גֵּט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing opinion within the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An impossible condition is treated as mere exaggeration and is ignored, so the גט is valid immediately.

steps.title: The הלכה follows רבי יהודה בן תימא
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן, quoting רב, rules like רבי יהודה בן תימא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said in the name of רב: The הלכה is like רבי יהודה בן תימא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the practical ruling in the dispute. The הלכה follows רבי יהודה בן תימא, so the גט is valid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This settles the disagreement between the תנא קמא and רבי יהודה בן תימא. In practice, a גט with an impossible condition works, and the condition is simply ignored.

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman said that Rav said:
The halakha follows Rabbi Yehuda ben Teima.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַב: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן תֵּימָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides the dispute presented in the previous two steps.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A גט given on an impossible condition is valid, because the condition is ignored.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical הלכה for any agreement made with a condition that can never be fulfilled.

steps.title: The wording of the משנה supports this ruling
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק points out that the משנה says a condition 'that can be fulfilled' stands. That implies a condition that cannot be fulfilled is cancelled.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: The משנה is also precise this way, because it teaches: Any condition that can be fulfilled in the end, which he set from the start, stands. This implies that if it cannot be fulfilled, the condition is cancelled. Learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק brings support for the ruling from a careful reading of a משנה about conditions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה limits its rule to conditions that 'can be fulfilled.' The extra detail implies the opposite case: an impossible condition does not stand. That is exactly רבי יהודה בן תימא's view, that the condition falls away and the deal goes through.

keyTerms.meaning: Is also precise (its wording supports this)

steps.confusionAlert: 'תנאו בטל' does not mean the גט is cancelled. Only the condition is cancelled, so the גט works without it.

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said:
The mishna is also precise in this way,
as it teaches:
any condition that can be fulfilled in the end,
and he set it as a condition from the start —
his condition stands;
this implies that if it cannot be fulfilled, his condition is cancelled;
learn from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the ruling of the previous step with an inference from the wording of a משנה.
steps.raayaObject: The ruling that the הלכה follows רבי יהודה בן תימא.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The wording of the משנה: 'any condition that can be fulfilled... his condition stands,' which implies that an impossible condition is cancelled.

steps.title: What about a condition to eat pig meat?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether a condition to eat חזיר counts as an impossible condition.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: If he says, "This is your גט on condition that you eat pig meat," what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new question and sets up the next two answers. Eating חזיר is physically possible, but the תורה forbids it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is whether 'impossible' covers only things that cannot physically be done, or also things that are forbidden. If forbidden counts as impossible, the condition is ignored and the גט works right away.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked among them

phrases.english: A question was raised before them:
"This is your bill of divorce
on condition that you eat pig meat,"
what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: הֲרֵי זֶה גִּיטִּיךְ עַל מְנָת שֶׁתֹּאכְלִי בְּשַׂר חֲזִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the rule about impossible conditions by testing a case that is forbidden but physically possible.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a condition that is forbidden by the תורה counts as 'impossible' under רבי יהודה בן תימא's rule.

steps.title: אביי: it is the same as an impossible condition
steps.stepSummary: אביי says a forbidden condition is just like an impossible one.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: It is the same.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the question. A condition to do something forbidden is treated like a condition that cannot be done.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For אביי, something the תורה forbids counts as impossible. So the condition is ignored, and the גט is valid right away.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
It is the same.
phrases.notes: Meaning it is the same as the impossible conditions in the ברייתא, like going up to the sky.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of the previous step.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A forbidden condition counts as impossible, so the condition is void and the גט is valid.

steps.title: רבא: it is possible, because she can eat it and get lashes
steps.stepSummary: רבא disagrees and says the condition can be fulfilled, even though doing it would be a sin.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: It is possible, since she can eat it and receive lashes.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a different answer. Eating חזיר is something she can actually do, even though she would be punished for it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבא, 'impossible' means only something that physically cannot happen. Since she is able to eat the meat, this is a real condition. The גט depends on whether she fulfills it.
steps.whatToRemember: Impossible conditions are ignored, and the גט is valid (the הלכה follows רבי יהודה בן תימא). For a forbidden condition, אביי treats it as impossible, while רבא says it is possible, because she can do it and be punished.

phrases.english: Rava said:
It is possible, since she can eat it and be flogged.
phrases.notes: Eating חזיר is a sin punished with lashes, but nothing physically stops her from doing it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an answer to the same question that disagrees with אביי.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A forbidden condition is still possible to fulfill, so it is a real condition and is not ignored.

steps.title: Which word each side relies on
steps.stepSummary: אביי learns from the word 'כלל' that בשר חזיר is included as an impossible condition. רבא learns from the word 'כזה' that it is excluded.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to אביי, the word 'principle' comes to include a condition of eating pig meat. According to רבא, the words 'like this' come to exclude pig meat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows how both אביי and רבא find support for their view in the wording of רבי יהודה בן תימא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי says the word 'כלל' (from 'כלל אמר רבי יהודה בן תימא') widens the rule beyond physically impossible conditions, so a forbidden condition like eating בשר חזיר also counts as impossible. רבא says the limiting word 'כזה' (from 'כזה – גט') narrows the rule to truly impossible conditions only, so בשר חזיר is left out. Each side builds on a different word in the same teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: A general principle; a word that widens the rule
Like this; a word that limits the rule

steps.confusionAlert: Both sides agree on the words of רבי יהודה בן תימא. They only argue about which of those words teaches the lesson.

phrases.english: According to Abaye, 'principle' comes to include pig meat.
phrases.notes: 'Principle' points to how רבי יהודה בן תימא opened his rule: 'כלל אמר', he stated a principle.

phrases.english: According to Rava, 'like this' comes to exclude pig meat.
phrases.notes: This points to his opening words 'כזה – גט', a case like this is a valid גט.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the textual basis for each side of the dispute in steps 18-19.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אביי: 'כלל' includes בשר חזיר as impossible. רבא: 'כזה' excludes it, so it is possible.

steps.title: A ברייתא about conditions involving relations
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא. A condition to have relations with 'so-and-so' is binding. A condition NOT to have relations with my father or your father raises no worry.
steps.simpleTranslation: They objected from a ברייתא: 'This is your גט on condition that you have relations with so-and-so.' If the condition is fulfilled, it is a גט, and if not, it is not a גט. If he says, 'On condition that you do not have relations with my father or your father,' we do not worry that perhaps she had relations with them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to challenge רבא. This step only quotes the source; the actual challenge comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא treats the 'so-and-so' condition as a real condition that the גט depends on. It also mentions the father-in-law and father, but only as a negative condition. That sets up the question of why the positive version is missing.

keyTerms.meaning: They raised an objection (from a תנאי source)

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
'This is your bill of divorce
on condition that you have relations with so-and-so,'
if the condition was fulfilled, it is a bill of divorce,
and if not, it is not a bill of divorce.
'On condition that you not have relations with my father or your father':
we are not concerned that perhaps she had relations with them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings an outside source to test רבא's view from step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's view that a forbidden condition counts as possible
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Setup only: the ברייתא's list of cases will be used in the next step to show what it leaves out.

steps.title: The missing father case challenges רבא
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא never teaches a positive condition to have relations with my father or your father. That fits אביי but is hard for רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: But 'on condition that you have relations with my father or your father' is not taught. For אביי this works well; for רבא it is difficult!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out what the ברייתא leaves out and uses that silence to attack רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a forbidden condition still counts as a real condition, as רבא holds, the ברייתא should have listed the father case alongside 'so-and-so.' Leaving it out suggests that such a forbidden condition is void, which is exactly what אביי says.

phrases.english: Whereas 'on condition that you have relations with my father or your father'
is not taught;
according to Abaye it works well; according to Rava it is difficult!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge set up by the ברייתא in step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling that a condition requiring a sin is still a valid, binding condition
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא skips the forbidden father case. That implies it is not a binding condition, which matches אביי and contradicts רבא.

steps.title: רבא: the father case is truly impossible
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that בשר חזיר and 'so-and-so' are within her power. The father case depends on other men, who will not sin, so it really is impossible.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא could tell you: Granted, with pig meat she can eat it and be lashed. With so-and-so too, she can bribe him with money. But my father or your father, is that in her hands?! Even if she would commit a sin, would my father or your father commit a sin?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא defends himself. He explains that the ברייתא left out the father case because it is a truly impossible condition, not merely a forbidden one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's rule is that a forbidden act still counts as possible if the woman herself can do it, even though she would sin and be punished. The father case is different because it depends on the cooperation of the fathers, who will surely refuse to sin. So it is a truly impossible condition, and even רבא agrees it is void.

keyTerms.meaning: He could say to you (a defense on someone's behalf)

steps.whatToRemember: For רבא, a condition is 'possible' if the woman herself can carry it out, even through a sin. It becomes 'impossible' when it depends on other people who will not sin.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sharpens רבא's view. The test is not whether the act is forbidden, but whether fulfilling it is in her own control.

phrases.english: Rava could say to you:
Granted with pig meat,
it is possible that she eats it and is lashed;

phrases.aramaic: פְּלוֹנִי נָמֵי – אֶפְשָׁר דִּמְשַׁחֲדָא לֵיהּ בְּמָמוֹנָא;
phrases.english: so-and-so too, it is possible that she bribes him with money;
but my father or your father, is it in her hands?!
Granted that she would commit a sin,
would my father or your father commit a sin?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 22 against רבא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases: something she can do herself versus something that depends on others
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The father case was left out because forbidden conditions are void, as אביי holds.
steps.terutzMaskana: The father case was left out because it is truly impossible: the fathers will not sin. רבא's rule for בשר חזיר still stands.

steps.title: How רבא reads 'כלל' and 'כזה'
steps.stepSummary: According to רבא, the word 'כלל' includes the 'my father and your father' condition as impossible, and the word 'כזה' excludes the בשר חזיר condition.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רבא: the word 'principle' comes to include 'my father and your father.' The words 'like this' come to exclude pig meat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wraps up רבא's view by showing what each extra word in the teaching of רבי יהודה בן תימא comes to teach, according to him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 23, רבא said the father case is truly impossible, since it depends on other men who will not sin. So now רבא has a use for the word 'כלל': it adds the father case to the list of impossible conditions. The word 'כזה' still does what it did in step 20: it leaves out בשר חזיר, which is in her own power and so counts as possible.

keyTerms.meaning: A general principle. Here it is the word רבי יהודה בן תימא used to open his rule, and the גמרא reads it as including extra cases.
'Like this.' The גמרא reads it as limiting the rule to cases like the one described.
To include, to bring in an extra case.
To exclude, to leave a case out.
'My father and your father.' This is the condition that she have relations with one of them.

steps.whatToRemember: אביי: 'כלל' includes בשר חזיר as impossible. רבא: 'כלל' includes the father case as impossible, and 'כזה' excludes בשר חזיר, which counts as possible.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two views of 'כלל.' For אביי it brings in בשר חזיר. For רבא it brings in the father case, and בשר חזיר is left out by 'כזה.'
steps.whyThisMatters: This finishes the defense of רבא. Every word in the teaching now has a job according to him, so his view stands even after the challenge from the ברייתא.

phrases.english: According to רבא, the word 'principle' comes to include 'my father and your father';
phrases.notes: 'Principle' is the word רבי יהודה בן תימא used to open his rule about impossible conditions.

phrases.english: the words 'like this' come to exclude pig meat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on רבא's answer in step 23. Since the father case is truly impossible, the גמרא now shows that רבא reads 'כלל' as including it.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבא has a full reading of the text. 'כלל' includes the father case as an impossible condition, and 'כזה' excludes בשר חזיר as a possible condition.
